newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's AWS says job cuts in coal-mining a must.
newsitem.headline: Poland's AWS says job cuts in coal-mining a must.

text.p: Poland's largest opposition party, the Solidarity Election Action (AWS) presented on Thursday a plan to restructure the ailing coal industry, which envisages cuts in jobs and broad social benefits for the sacked.

"Polish coal mining has an excessive production capacity... and relatively low effectiveness, which creates a necessity of labour reduction," Janusz Steinhoff, Solidarity expert told a news conference.
"The job reduction should be carried out in a civilised way, which means with a worker's consent and accompanied by substantial social security benefits," Steinhoff added.
Steinhoff said the current number of 240,000 workers employed by the coal industry would have to be reduced by 80,000 within the next ten years.

He added the cost of redundancy benefits and new job training incentives, to be financed from the state budget, would be lower than the industry's annual production losses and would not exceed 900 million zlotys ($257.3 million).
He said the industry's losses, stemming from high costs and low coal prices, would exceed 1.7 billion zlotys in 1997.
As part of the overhaul, the AWS also suggested to write off all the mines' debts to the treasury.
"The debts should be written off because the mines will not be able to pay them back anyway," Steinhoff said.
The mining sector's debt in 1996 reached 10.8 billion zlotys against 191.8 million zlotys in 1994 after the current government coalition took power.

The AWS, which groups more than 30 right wing parties around the Solidarity trade union, is running neck and neck with the ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance in opinion polls ahead of the September 21 parliamentary elections.
